podcast.body: This single was a significant hit for Earth Wind & Fire, reaching number 4 on the R&B chart and number 29 on the pop chart. It distilled the band's sound for radio, establishing a template of melodic funk characterized by brassy, intricate playing and stacked vocals. "Mighty Mighty, a number 4 R&B, number 29 pop hit, distilled the Earth Wind and Fire sound for radio domination, and set a template for the band."

podcast.body: This song, from their 1974 album *Open Our Eyes*, features the chorus "we are people of the mighty, mighty people of the sun." It achieved commercial success, reaching number 29 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 4 on the Billboard Hot Soul Charts. However, some radio stations refused to play it, believing it was associated with the Black Power movement, as noted by the band's founding members. Laurie Janelle Dance, an Assistant Professor of Sociology, recalled that listening to the song in the 70s helped her heal by declaring "black was beautiful," directly challenging the dominant culture's historical depiction of African Americans as inferior. "It helped to heal my wounds by declaring that black was beautiful."
